thread:
incident-bot: Pager: CitrineSystems (Private VPC, dedicated pool) — elevated 503 rate from tenant ingress via NLB. Trigger: NLB health check failures and downstream 5xxs. Paging oncall.

oncall-alex: on it, grabbing runbook. tagging neteng.

neteng-sumi: saw probe fail pattern from multiple AZs ~1735509000. NLB target group showing Unhealthy for backend-targets-asterion (10.4.x.x). Health check path /hc returns 200 locally.

se-ella: confirming app logs — spikes of connection reset/sock_errs around same window. No recent deploys for Citrine.

oncall-alex: @customer-citrine-sre can you confirm any config changes (SG, NACL, or sidecar) on your side?

customer-citrine-sre: Nothing changed from our end. We did rotate a cert yesterday but only for internal control-plane. No scaling. We see client 503s starting ~1735508800.

neteng-sumi: checking VPC-level SGs: there was a temporary tighten rule applied to restrict ephemeral ports yesterday — listing rules now.

neteng-sumi: ```
aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0abc1234 | jq '.IpPermissions'
# found rule: deny all ephemeral 32768-65535 TCP from 0.0.0.0/0 (intentional for audit)
```

eng-runtime-raj: that ephemeral block can break NLB target health if healthcheck responses require ephemeral outbound. NLB health checks are TCP 443 from LB to instance. If instance can't respond due to ephemeral restriction to downstream services, it might fail.

se-ella: app health handler calls an internal config fetch on 10.5.x.x:8080 — that fetch is outbound from service and uses ephemeral ports. If SG blocks ephemeral egress to internal config service, health handler times out -> 503.

oncall-alex: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) open ephemeral egress from backend to internal control plane for CITRINE tenant SG 2) temporarily mark affected targets unhealthy and failover traffic to dedicated ALB fallback 3) contact customer for maintenance window if we need longer change. Thoughts? :eyes:

neteng-sumi: I can patch SG to allow ephemeral 32768-61000 to 10.5.0.0/16 from the backend SG. Will push in 1m and monitor.

customer-citrine-sre: please do. We can tolerate a short window. We'll keep monitoring on our side.

eng-runtime-raj: also recommending increasing NLB healthcheck timeout from 3s -> 6s as a temporary tolerance to transient slowdowns. I can queue that change but prefer SG fix first.

incident-bot: ACTION ADDED: Allow ephemeral egress to control-plane / change SG (actor: neteng-sumi) — ETA 5m.

neteng-sumi: changes applied at 1735510100. Patch: opened TCP 32768-61000 to 10.5.0.0/16 on sg-0abc1234.

se-ella: app health endpoints now returning 200 on checks. Observed reduced 503s. Monitoring for 10m.

eng-runtime-raj: also switched NLB target group health check timeout to 6s at 1735510300 as belt-and-suspenders. Reverting once stable.

customer-citrine-sre: seeing traffic normalize, thank you. Any postmortem notes we should capture?

oncall-alex: immediate RCA: security group egress hardening blocked ephemeral ports required for app->control-plane health checks, causing application health probes to fail and NLB to mark targets unhealthy -> 503s. Remediation: revert tighten rule or scope to exclude backend SGs; increased NLB timeout to mitigate flapping. Next steps: schedule a config review + add healthcheck dependency map to runbook.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) at 1735511200. Close after 30m monitoring if no regression. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime-raj: follow-up: I'll add an integration test in infra CI that simulates healthcheck chain and alerts when ephemeral blocks are present.

customer-citrine-sre: appreciate the fast response. Please include us on the postmortem and any config changes.

oncall-alex: will create postmortem doc and ping owners. closing here once monitoring window passes. :thumbsup:
